title: Rule or exception? Judge a move without being told
outcomes: Decides whether a rule of thumb picks a good move in a position, with no label
Names the one feature that makes the rule hold in one position and fail in its twin
Checks first whether the rule governs the position at all
Writes a minimal pair of his own for a rule (paper exercise)

steps.text: The lesson *When the rule fails: test it with one change* showed pairs that were labelled. Now you get a rule and a move, and nothing says whether this is a case where the rule holds. Decide, then read the engine's check. *Rule of thumb:* a rule is a default; the board decides whether a feature cancels it.

Before you trust a rule, ask two things. Does it govern this position at all (is there a rook that can reach a file with no pawns, or a knight that can reach an outpost)? And if it does, which feature could cancel it: a piece that makes the move cost something. Compare the pair below with a position where the rule has no move to offer.

steps.title: The rule holds, the rule fails, no rule to apply
steps.prompt: Predict the answer in each position. The first two differ by one piece: name it and say what it changes. In the third, say why the rule of thumb is not in play.

Paper exercise (the app does not check it): choose one rule you use. Draw a position where it picks a good move, then change exactly one thing (move one piece) so that it picks a poor one. Write what you changed and why it matters. That pair is your own minimal pair; keep the rule and add its condition.
